trust_decision.summary: missingKeyHandler decides which attacker-supplied request-body keys are forwarded to backendConnector.saveMissing; at the pinned commit it rejects only the literal names __proto__/constructor/prototype, not keys whose keySeparator-split segments are those names.

landing_point.why: The summary names MissingKeyHandler; the only key filter in it is the literal UNSAFE_KEYS check on body keys.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API missingKeyHandler(i18next, options) mounted as an HTTP POST route (express/fastify/koa/hapi/custom via checkForCombinedReqRes)
new exported helper utils.hasUnsafeKeySegment, reached only via missingKeyHandler (inserted after lib/utils.js:44, fix.diff:55)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The fix's utils.js helper is new code called only from the handler; no second implementation, wrapper or lower-level API reaches saveMissing in this repo (lib/index.js:320 is the only saveMissing call).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 route: the advisory is about body keys, while lng/ns are route params the server developer defines, and lng/ns filtering was only ever applied in getResourcesHandler (lib/index.js:265-266), so the missing-key path looks like it was deliberately left alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate dotted keys (e.g. header.title) must still be saved; with a custom keySeparator (':') a '.'-containing key is one key and must be kept; with keySeparator=false only the literal denylist applies. A fix that bans any key containing __proto__ as a substring or always splits on '.' breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: literal unsafe key (__proto__, constructor, prototype), already handled at the pin
body given as an async function that returns the object (lib/index.js:324-333), which goes through the same saveMissingKeys

O7_producer.where: The segment splitting that turns the key into a path happens in external backends (i18next-fs-backend writeFile per fix.diff:12), outside this repo; the only in-repo config read is i18next.options.keySeparator (fix.diff:25).

O8_uncovered_routes.route: missingKeyHandler forwards route params lng and ns to saveMissing unvalidated, so a __proto__/constructor/prototype lng or ns reaches the same backend write that the body-key check guards.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and its fix deal only with body keys; lng/ns come from a developer-defined route, and the identifier filters exist only in getResourcesHandler (lib/index.js:265-266).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Same function, about 17 lines above the landing point (lib/index.js:302 vs lib/index.js:319); the matching filter helpers are in lib/utils.js:24-40.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second missing-key entry, e.g. a batched or multi-namespace variant that loops over body[ns] objects and keeps the old literal-only UNSAFE_KEYS check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handler already takes getBody as either an object or an async function (lib/index.js:324-336), so a maintainer adding a batch shape could easily copy the pre-fix loop.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A setPath-style helper that splits a dotted key and also maps '###' back to '.' after the unsafe-key check, giving a rename-after-check differential.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: setPath already does the ### -> . replacement before its guard (lib/utils.js:53-54); writing the guard before the replacement is a plausible maintainer ordering mistake.

O9_family: prototype pollution (CWE-1321) via a key-path segment denylist gap

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm; babel, mocha, expect.js, eslint, tsd (package.json:30-57, package.json:81)
O10_build.project_tests: test/security.js:61-86 (missingKeyHandler literal-key test using a fake backendConnector); test/missingKeyHandler.{express,fastify,koa,hapi,custom}.js

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Split on a hard-coded '.' (ignoring i18next.options.keySeparator / false), or reject any key containing '__proto__' as a substring, and leave lng/ns unchecked.

out_of_scope_notes: The root cause is in downstream backends (i18next-fs-backend writeFile setPath, per fix.diff:12), a different repository.
nsSeparator-prefixed keys (e.g. 'ns:__proto__.x') may be interpreted differently by i18next core/backends; not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured; tiny_repo is inferred from lib/ having 9 source files (lib/index.js is 383 lines).
Whether the latest release validates lng/ns in missingKeyHandler is unknown (no latest tree provided).
Whether downstream backends treat a __proto__ lng/ns as a prototype-polluting path (vs only a file path) was not checked in this repo.
Advisory text itself was not provided; the trust decision is based on the fix diff and CHANGELOG entry in it (fix.diff:12).
